chunks: 4199 - Al-Washsha narrated from Dawud Al-Raqqi, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man from the companions of Abū al-Khaṭṭāb forbade me from the Bukht and from eating the meat of musarwal pigeons.

So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "There is no harm in riding the Bukht, drinking their milk, eating their meat, and eating the meat of musarwal pigeons." And he عليه السلام forbade riding the jallālāt and drinking their milk, and said: "If anything from their sweat touches you, then wash it."
And the jallālah she-camel is tied up for forty days, then after that its slaughter and eating become permissible; and the cow is tied up for thirty days.

key_terms.النَّاقَةُ الْجَلَّالَةُ: a jallālah she-camel that must be confined forty days before slaughter and eating
key_terms.الْبَقَرَةُ: the cow, which if jallālah is confined for thirty days
key_terms.الْبُخْتِ: a kind of camel whose riding, milk, and meat are ruled permissible here
key_terms.الْجَلَّالَاتِ: animals that feed on filth, whose riding and milk are prohibited in this report
key_terms.الْحَمَامِ الْمُسَرْوَلِ: pigeons with feathered legs whose meat is ruled permissible
key_terms.عَرَقِهَا: the sweat of such animals, which must be washed if it touches a person

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on riding and consuming Bukht camels, musarwal pigeons, and jallālah animals in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the permissibility of riding and consuming certain animals, including Bukht camels and musarwal pigeons. It also prohibits using and consuming from jallālah animals until they are confined for a set period, and instructs washing off their sweat if it touches a person. The report reflects fiqh rulings related to halal and haram, animal impurity, and purification.
